When Charles Grandison Finney was converted
column2: In 1821 Finney experienced a soul-shattering conversion that led him to give up his law practice and become an itinerant minister.

column1: When Finney's Erie Canal revivals drew national attention
column2: Finney conducted spectacular revivals in booming Erie Canal port cities in the mid-1820s and early 1830s, including Rochester in the winter of 1830–1831.

column1: When the AME Church was organized, and how large it grew
column2: The African Methodist Episcopal Church was organized at Philadelphia in 1816, and by 1856 it boasted some 20,000 members.

column1: The usual ratio of female to male revival converts
column2: In most revivals, female converts outnumbered males by about three to two.

column1: How widespread church membership was by 1840
column2: By 1840 an estimated half of the adult population was connected to some church, and the Methodists had become the largest Protestant denomination.

column1: American liquor consumption in 1825 and by 1845
column2: By 1825 the average American over 15 drank over five gallons of distilled liquor a year, the highest level in American history and nearly triple present-day levels, but by 1845 consumption had fallen below two gallons a year.

column1: When the American Temperance Society was founded
column2: The American Temperance Society was founded in 1826, and about 5,000 local societies formed in the next decade.

column1: When the Maine Law was passed
column2: The Maine Law, the first statewide prohibition law, was passed in 1851, and similar laws followed in a number of states, though most were later struck down or repealed.

column1: When anti-Catholic violence erupted in Charlestown and Philadelphia
column2: A Charlestown, Massachusetts, mob burned a convent in 1834, and two outbreaks of anti-Catholic violence in Philadelphia in the summer of 1844 left 14 people dead.

column1: When Emerson delivered the Divinity School Address and "The American Scholar"
column2: Emerson issued a declaration of literary independence in "The American Scholar" in 1837 and delivered the Divinity School Address in July 1838.

column1: When major works of the American Renaissance appeared
column2: Hawthorne's The Scarlet Letter appeared in 1850, Melville's Moby-Dick in 1851, Thoreau's Walden in 1854 after 16 months at Walden Pond beginning in 1845, and Whitman's Leaves of Grass in 1855.

column1: When Robert Owen's New Harmony experiment ended
column2: Owen's New Harmony community in Indiana attracted about 900 volunteers and dissolved in 1827.

column1: The peak size of the Shakers and of Oneida
column2: The Shakers peaked at about 6,000 members, and the Oneida Community grew to more than 200 members in 1851 before falling apart after Noyes lost power in 1879 and reorganizing as a business in 1881.

column1: When Joseph Smith was murdered and the Mormons moved west
column2: Smith was murdered in 1844; the Mormons left Nauvoo, which had reached a population of 10,000 by the mid-1840s, in 1846, and Brigham Young led them to Utah in 1847.

column1: When The Liberator first appeared
column2: William Lloyd Garrison published the first issue of The Liberator on January 1, 1831.

column1: When Britain ended the slave trade and then freed its colonial slaves
column2: Parliament outlawed the British slave trade in 1808, emancipated nearly 800,000 slaves in 1833, and freed nearly 800,000 slaves in its colonies in 1834.

column1: When the American Anti-Slavery Society was founded, and how large it grew
column2: Abolitionists founded the New England Anti-Slavery Society in 1832 and the American Anti-Slavery Society in 1833, and about 200,000 northerners belonged to the movement.

column1: When a Boston mob seized Garrison and when Elijah Lovejoy was murdered
column2: A Boston mob seized Garrison in 1835, and Elijah Lovejoy was murdered in Alton, Illinois, in 1837.

column1: When the Seneca Falls convention met
column2: In 1848 Stanton and Mott organized a conference at Seneca Falls, New York, that attracted about a hundred supporters and issued the Declaration of Sentiments.

column1: When abolitionists split and when the Liberty Party first ran
column2: In 1840 the movement split after Garrison packed an American Anti-Slavery Society convention on the question of women holding office, and the Liberty Party nominated James Birney, who received about 7,000 votes.

column1: When the gag rule was adopted and repealed
column2: The House adopted the gag rule in 1836, automatically tabling antislavery petitions, and repealed it in 1844 after abolitionists used the issue to defend white civil liberties.

column1: When abolitionists mailed more than a million pamphlets
column2: In 1835 abolitionists mailed more than a million pamphlets, a campaign that helped provoke southern demands for censorship of the mails and the gag rule.
